Both edit the identical write_stream construction line and would conflict on merge. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the ENTIRE header (not just the portion after the first space) and _extract_bearer_auth_params then scans segments to locate the Bearer scheme boundary, so it correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space and treats everything after it as a single challenge's params, so it would misparse multi-scheme headers by folding a subsequent scheme's tokens into the Bearer param list. #3041's approach covers a strict superset of the cases #3012 handles.

prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string-valued argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`. For `str | None` (and similar unions), this corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "true", "123", "null", "[1,2]") by decoding them into bool/int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes any string-valued argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`. For `str | None` (and similar unions), this corrupts legitimate string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. "true", "123", "null", "[1,2]") by decoding them into bool/int/None/list before Pydantic validation ever sees the original string. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same isinstance/annotation check in pre_parse_json to stop pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` tests union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str, int, float, bool, NoneType). That membership test fails for the common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern, since `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not identical to the bare `str` type object, so it falls through to 'not simple' and pre-parsing (and the corruption bug) still occurs for annotated Optional[str] parameters, which is the idiomatic way to declare a described optional string in FastMCP. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated[...]` before the union check, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly recognized and skipped. #3056 is also narrower in scope (only `str | None`), leaving pre-parsing behavior for other simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool` unchanged, whereas #2032 silently changes coercion behavior for those unions too as a side effect of its broader rule.

prs.author: app/claude
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a restart, `OAuthContext.oauth_metadata` is empty in memory (only tokens are persisted), so refreshing a token has no reliable way to resolve the authorization server's token endpoint. #2492 ('...to fix refresh after restart') solves this by persisting metadata through new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods on `TokenStorage`. #3263 ('discover AS metadata before cold-start token refresh...') solves the identical scenario by re-running discovery on demand before a cold-start refresh, guarded by an `eager_discovery_attempted` flag. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same isinstance/annotation check in pre_parse_json to stop pre-parsing for str-containing unions, but #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` tests union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare types: str, int, float, bool, NoneType). That membership test fails for the common `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern, since `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not identical to the bare `str` type object, so it falls through to 'not simple' and pre-parsing (and the corruption bug) still occurs for annotated Optional[str] parameters, which is the idiomatic way to declare a described optional string in FastMCP. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated` specifically to strip `Annotated[...]` before the union check, so `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` is correctly recognized and skipped. #3056 is also narrower in scope (only `str | None`), leaving pre-parsing behavior for other simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool` unchanged, whereas #2032 silently changes coercion behavior for those unions too as a side effect of its broader rule.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both target the same root cause: write_stream is created with a zero-capacity memory object stream, so send() on it rendezvous-blocks until the reader picks up the message. This causes stalls when a handler needs to queue a final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 exposes read/write buffer sizes as constructor parameters but leaves the default at 0, so the blocking behavior is unchanged unless a caller opts in and explicitly sets write_stream_buffer_size. #2654 hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 at the same call site, fixing the blocking behavior by default, and adds a regression test (BlockingStdout) that reproduces the stall during a slow stdout flush. Both edit the identical write_stream construction line and would conflict on merge.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962 is tied to filed issue #2960 and cites SEP-1577's actual text ('tool_result blocks MUST be preceded by a tool_use block, but there is NO requirement that a tool_use MUST be [followed by tool_result]') as the justification for making this a non-error case, and its regression test asserts validate_tool_use_result_messages does not raise. #3053 takes the opposite stance (still raises, only reword the message) without referencing the spec, so it directly conflicts with #2962's behavior on the same input rather than complementing it — merging both is impossible since the second `if` in #3053 would be unreachable dead code once #2962's `has_tool_results and` guard is applied. Given #2962 is spec-referenced and has an explicit regression test for this exact scenario, it should be kept and #3053 closed as superseded.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs edit the same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that fires when an assistant message's tool_use blocks are not matched by tool_result blocks in the following message, but they resolve it with opposite, mutually exclusive behavior: #2962 changes the guard to `has_tool_results and has_previous_tool_use and previous_content`, which skips the id-matching check entirely (no exception) when there are no tool_result blocks at all. #3053 keeps the check active and instead inserts an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` with a clearer message, i.e. it still raises in that case, just with different wording than the original 'ids ... do not match' error. clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the ENTIRE header (not just the portion after the first space) and _extract_bearer_auth_params then scans segments to locate the Bearer scheme boundary, so it correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds the first space and treats everything after it as a single challenge's params, so it would misparse multi-scheme headers by folding a subsequent scheme's tokens into the Bearer param list. #3041's approach covers a strict superset of the cases #3012 handles.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same root cause in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/first-space splitting that broke when auth-param values contained commas or other schemes appeared in the same header, causing incorrect extraction of fields like 'error' or 'realm'. Each PR introduces a quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer to replace the substring-based logic.
